content.title: MyLiaison - University of California-Irvine
content.text: The University of California, Irvine (UCI) is a renowned public research university located in Irvine, California. Established in 1965, UCI is one of the ten campuses of the University of California system. The university's mission is to serve as a catalyst for societal change and academic excellence through its dedication to research, scholarship, and community engagement.UCI offers a diverse range of undergraduate and graduate programs across various disciplines. The campus is known for its top-ranked programs in engineering, biological sciences, computer science, business, social sciences, and the arts. The university also boasts exceptional research facilities and centers, such as the Beckman Laser Institute, the Center for the Neurobiology of Learning and Memory, and the Advanced Power and Energy Program.Beyond academics, UCI is renowned for its commitment to sustainability and green initiatives. The campus features sustainable buildings, energy conservation efforts, and eco-friendly transportation systems. UCI is also home to numerous student organizations, clubs, and sports teams that provide students with opportunities for social engagement and personal growth. With its beautiful campus, strong academic reputation, and commitment to research and sustainability, UCI offers a vibrant and inclusive community for students to thrive. Located in Irvine, CA, University of California, Irvine is a public university. This academic institution uses a quarterly calendar. It has an acceptance rate of 28%. The freshman retention rate at University of California, Irvine is 94.2% and the six-year graduation rate is 87%. For freshmen, the application deadline for this school is November 30. Discover more about what you can expect if you get into University of California, Irvine. Quick Facts 30,204 Total Number of Undergraduate Students Admissions Knowing as much as possible about the institution's criteria for admission increases your chances of getting admitted. Learn some vital facts about admission policy and requirements at University of California, Irvine. In 2025, the school accepted 35,317 new students. Deadlines The deadline for submitting applications to University of California, Irvine is November 30. Retention Rate The percentage of first-year students at a college or university who stay on for their second year is known as the freshman retention rate. When you make your list of possible schools to attend, you should consider the freshman retention rate, among other things. The freshman retention rate for University of California, Irvine was 94.2% in 2025, which is an outstanding retention rate only the most prestigious institutions have. Another important metric to consider is the graduation rate. This rate indicates how many students finish their degrees within a certain timeframe. At this school, the rate of students graduating within six years is 87%, which is considered an above-average graduation rate. Student Body Figuring out which school is the right fit for you is not a task you should take lightly. You can better understand the culture and life of the school by learning more about the student body. Main Student Body In 2025, the institution had an enrollment of 37,296 students. That year, the school had an out-of-state student body percentage of 8. The total number of undergraduate students enrolled at the school was 30,204, 3714 of which were foreign students. The number of transfer students at this school was 2,719. Student Population Gender Ratio The student body is coeducational, with 15,838 male and 19,634 female full-time students in 2025, which is indicative of the importance this institution places on gender equality. Student Population Diversity When it comes to improving a sense of inclusion and belonging among students, there is no denying the importance of student diversity. Diversity promotes critical thinking, challenges preconceived notions, and encourages intellectual growth, so it helps students develop empathy and a broader understanding of the world. Find out more about different ethnic groups you can meet at University of California, Irvine. In 2025, out of the total number of students enrolled at the institution, the number of Asian students was 11,316, and the number of African American students was 590. 8,105 students at this school declared as Hispanic/Latino and 1,903 as multirace. The school also had 24 students who identified as Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander, and 42 American Indian or Alaska Native students. There were also 654 students whose ethnicity is unknown. Cost One of the most crucial things to take into account when applying to any college or university is the financial component. Here are some details you should know about the cost of attendance for University of California, Irvine. Tuition and Fees Here are some facts that can be useful if you were curious about University of California, Irvine estimated tuition costs. If you are an area resident, your tuition was $13,602. Tuition fees were $51,204 for students coming from out of state. For international students, tuition fees at this school came to $51,204, as well. Full-time students in 2025 needed to pay additional fees in the amount of $2,798. Books and Supplies When you try to estimate the cost of attendance for a college or university, you need to take into account the cost of books and supplies you're going to need. The approximate cost of books and supplies for full-time students of this school is $1,543. Boarding Before you apply to a college or university, you should, among other things, think about the price of a dorm room and cafeteria meals. How much do room and board fees average around at schools? The cost of room and board (on campus) per academic year at University of California, Irvine was $19,653 in 2025. Financial Aid Be it a grant, loan, scholarship, or work-study program, any type of financial aid can be a great deal for a number of students. If you want to find out more about need-based and non-need-based aid at University of California, Irvine, here are some recent data you should consider. The most recent figures show that financial help was given to 3,229 freshmen. The average amount of financial aid given to students was $27,265. Need-based Financial aid that a student can receive if they are determined to have financial need and meet other eligibility requirements is known as need-based aid. 15,032 students were granted some form of need-based financial aid. Need-based college-administered scholarship and grant aid at University of California, Irvine isn't available to international students. The total number of students (including freshmen) who were determined to have financial need was estimated to be 15,798. The amount of federal need-based scholarships/grants awarded to the students at this institution stood at $72,544,305, and state $152,160,197. The students of University of California, Irvine received the -institutional need-based aid in the amount of $137,570,376, and external in the amount of $3,837,164. $10,188 Average Amount of Aid Received Non-Need Based Non-need-based financial aid is any type of financial aid provided to a student who does not meet the criteria for need-based aid. The most popular forms of non-need-based financial aid for students are loans and grants, like Direct Unsubsidized Stafford Loans, Graduate PLUS Loans, Parent PLUS Loans, and the Teacher Education Access for College and Higher Education (TEACH) Grant. Institutional non-need-based scholarships or grants were given to 472 students overall (including freshmen) at University of California, Irvine in 2025. Institutional help in the form of non-need-based scholarships or grants was given to 149 full-time freshmen. Federal non-need-based scholarships and grants totaled $72,544,305 for students at this institution, while state aid came to $1,207,888. The total amount of non-need-based institutional scholarships/grants was $13,339,219. This includes endowment, alumni, other institutional awards, and also external funds awarded by the institution, but doesn't include athletic aid and tuition waivers. $4,152,940 was the amount that the students at this institution got from external sources (like Kiwanis and National Merit). Majors Campus Life Knowing what to expect out of campus life at a college or university can set you up for success. Check out some details about students' life at University of California, Irvine. Student Organizations A student organization is run by students at a university or a college institution, whose membership typically consists only of current students and/or alumni. Students interested in music can join the University of California, Irvine band or chorus. There is a drama club you can join if acting is something that interests you. Interested in media and communication? University of California, Irvine publishes its own newspaper and has its own radio station. Career Services Having career services at a college or university can mean a great deal for your career planning, so find out what you can expect at University of California, Irvine. Career Counselling This school offers alumni networking opportunities, which could be excellent for your future career. FAQ University of California, Irvine is located in Irvine, CA. University of California, Irvine doesn't offer need-based college-administered scholarship and grant aid to international students. The most recent reported acceptance rate for University of California, Irvine is 28%. The most recent data indicate that the freshman retention rate for University of California, Irvine is 94.2%.
